note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
“when money failed in the land of Egypt,” all the Egyptians came to Joseph and said, “Give us bread: for why should we die in thy presence? for the money faileth.” Listen to that: money failed. What good is money in a time of famine? It is useless. The first year they gave their cattle for bread. The second year there was “not ought left in the sight of my lord, but our bodies, and our lands,” so they said, “buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants unto Pharaoh.” “so the land became Pharaoh’s.”

Don't think that can never happen again. The things written aforetime were written for our learning. The Agenda 21 plan is total collectivism: people dependent on the state for everything, no private property or land of their own, housed in high-rise apartments provided as a benefit, because anyone with a couple of acres, his own water and his own food is a threat to it. BlackRock and Blackstone are buying up housing across America and controlling the rents. It is Genesis 47 again: take care of us, and we will give up everything. And as KRS-One said, we never lost our lands, we lost our minds; the intellectuals stay quiet because the paycheck dictates what comes out of the mind.

Daniel shows the hour it is: “And in the latter time of their kingdom, when the transgressors are come to the full, a king of fierce countenance, and understanding dark sentences, shall stand up.” That is the era we are in now. There are people in this administration studying the scriptures, reading from sunup to sundown and taking notes. Psalms 64:6 says it: “they accomplish a diligent search.”

While you struggle to do your four chapters a day, they have made study their job. While the grocery stores move out of our communities and Section 8 is taken away, too many of our people are still playing with adultery and lies. God has no time for that.

Egypt in Joseph's day sold itself to Pharaoh for bread; the spiritual Egypt will be given over into the hand of a cruel lord.

precepts.text: Joseph placed his father and his brethren in the best of the land and nourished them; the dream was fulfilled.
precepts.point: The dream came true. In the famine the whole house of Jacob came down to Joseph in Egypt, and he placed them in the best of the land and nourished them with bread; they bowed to the one the Most High had set over them.

note.label: Genesis 37: Joseph the Dreamer

precepts.why:
“And Joseph placed his father and his brethren, and gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded. And Joseph nourished his father, and his brethren, and all his father’s household, with bread”.

The dream came true. In the famine the whole house of Jacob came down to Joseph in Egypt, and he placed them in the best of the land and nourished them with bread. The sun, the moon and the eleven stars bowed to the one the Most High had set over them.

precepts.text: Moses was shown the secrets of the times and the end; that is how the land carried the name Rameses in the writing.
precepts.point: Rameses was the king at the time Israel left Egypt, and Moses wrote the first five books of the Bible; he wrote the place under the name of his own day. In the bush the Most High manifestly revealed himself to Moses, showed him the secrets of the times and the end, the beginning to the end, and the words were written again with Esdras.

note.label: Genesis 47: Goshen, the Famine, and the Fifth Part

precepts.why:
“In the bush I did manifestly reveal myself unto Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt: And I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to the mount of where I held him by me a long season, And told him many wondrous things, and shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end; and commanded him, saying, These words shalt thou declare, and these shalt thou hide.”

Moses wrote the first five books of the Bible, and the Most High showed him the secrets of the times and the end, the beginning to the end. So when Moses wrote that Joseph placed his father and his brethren “in the land of Rameses”, he wrote the place under the name of his own day: Rameses was the king at the time Israel left Egypt. Goshen and the land of Rameses are the exact same place.

And the words were written again with Esdras, which is how we have them.

precepts.text: By faith Jacob blessed the sons of Joseph, and by faith Joseph gave commandment concerning his bones.
precepts.point: Neither was there a man born like unto Joseph, a governor of his brethren, a stay of the people, whose bones were regarded of the Lord. To grow in spirit and be like him, put on the spirit of the forefathers.

note.label: Genesis 47: Goshen, the Famine, and the Fifth Part

precepts.why:
“By faith Jacob, when he was a dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph; and worshipped, leaning upon the top of his staff. By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Israel; and gave commandment concerning his bones.”

That is this scene: Israel, with the time drawn nigh that he must die, making Joseph swear to carry him out of Egypt and bury him in the buryingplace of his fathers, and bowing himself upon the bed’s head. It was faith. And Joseph took the same faith to his own death, making mention of the departing of the children of Israel and giving commandment concerning his bones.

Hebrews 11 is the hall of faith, the faithful men of the sons of God, a chapter to read.

precepts.text: No man was born like unto Joseph; put on the spirit of the forefathers.
precepts.point: Neither was there a man born like unto Joseph, a governor of his brethren, a stay of the people, whose bones were regarded of the Lord. To grow in spirit and be like him, put on the spirit of the forefathers.

note.label: Genesis 47: Goshen, the Famine, and the Fifth Part

precepts.why:
“Neither was there a young man born like Joseph, a governor of his brethren, a stay of the people, whose bones were regarded of the Lord.” No man was born like unto Joseph. He governed his brethren, he was the stay of the people through the famine, and his bones were regarded of the Lord, the bones he gave commandment about as his father gave commandment about his own burial here.

To grow in spirit and be like him, put on the spirit of the forefathers.

precepts.text: Goshen, the best of the land, was given to Israel in Joseph's day; that is where the children of Israel dwelt apart from Egypt.
precepts.point: Goshen was Israel's own quarter in Egypt, where we had our own houses and our own cattle; it was given to us in the days of Joseph, as we read in the book of Genesis.

note.label: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice, and Swarms of Flies

precepts.why:
“I will sever in that day the land of Goshen, in which my people dwell, that no swarms of flies shall be there”. Goshen was Israel's own quarter in Egypt, where we had our own houses and our own cattle.

It was given to us in the days of Joseph: Pharaoh said, “The land of Egypt is before thee; in the best of the land make thy father and brethren to dwell; in the land of Goshen let them dwell”. That is where the children of Israel dwelt apart from Egypt, and that is where the Lord put a division between His people and Pharaoh's people, so that Pharaoh would know that the Lord is in the midst of the earth.
